definition: The 2011 edition of the C programming language standard. It defines language and library rules while still leaving some target and implementation choices explicit.
A C construct that introduces a name and its type or other properties. A declaration can also define an object and give it an initial value.
The value or list of values supplied when an object is created in C. It establishes starting contents before later operations use them.
A region of data storage whose contents can represent values. Access must respect the object type, lifetime and permitted operations.
The language description of a value or object, including which representations and operations apply. An ordinary integer type does not enforce an application-specific physical unit.
A named input declared by a function. A normal C function call passes argument values into its parameters.
An expression supplied in a function call. Its value is used to initialise the corresponding parameter according to the language rules.
A named library interface included with a preprocessor include directive. Standard headers make the relevant declarations, macros and type names available.
A C program running in an environment that provides the hosted standard-library facilities and starts execution through main. A microcontroller build can use a different, freestanding environment.
A value representing false or true. C11 provides the bool name and true/false macros through stdbool.h.
An integer type representing non-negative values. Unsigned conversion reduces an out-of-range integer into the destination range rather than reporting an application range error.
An integer type that represents negative and non-negative values within a specified range. C does not generally define ordinary signed arithmetic overflow as wraparound.

An integer type with exactly the named bit width and no padding bits. Unsigned variants use the full width for value bits; signed variants include a sign bit and require two’s-complement representation in C11. The names exist only when the implementation supports the required representation.
A bit in an integer object representation that is not used to represent the numeric value. Exact-width integer types exclude padding bits.
Changing an integer value to another integer type. The destination range and signedness determine what happens when the value cannot be represented unchanged.
An explicit C request to convert an expression to a named type. A cast does not prove that the application intended the resulting value or that a fabricated pointer is valid.
A C type qualifier that restricts modification through the qualified access. It does not on its own choose flash storage or make other objects immutable.
A language conversion that can turn a smaller integer type into int or unsigned int before an operation. It means an operation on a small integer may use a wider promoted type.
A signed arithmetic result outside the representable range of its type. Ordinary signed arithmetic overflow has undefined behaviour in C11.
A case where the C standard imposes no requirements on the program behaviour. A seemingly successful test does not make an invalid operation reliable.

A C value of a pointer-to-object type that can refer to an object. It can also be null or point one past an array's end; neither permits accessing an element there. Access requires the proper type, alignment, lifetime and permissions; keeping a pointer does not extend an object's lifetime.
The unary C operator written & that obtains the address of an appropriate operand. In an expression with two integer operands, the same symbol instead denotes bitwise AND.
Accessing the object referred to by an object pointer, commonly using unary * in C. Dereferencing an invalid, misaligned or expired pointer is not permitted.
The placement requirements for an object of a particular type at an address. A pointer value that does not satisfy the type alignment requirements is not a valid basis for that access.
An independent stored copy of a value obtained at a particular access. Later changes to the source do not automatically update that copy.
A device interface where accesses to specified addresses communicate with peripheral registers. Device documentation defines access widths, ordering requirements and side effects.

A C qualifier used for objects whose accesses have significance beyond ordinary computation, under the implementation access rules. It does not supply atomic updates, mutual exclusion or a memory barrier.
An operation that is indivisible with respect to the relevant observers under its defined execution model. A volatile read-modify-write expression is not automatically such an operation.
A mechanism with specified ordering effects on memory operations. Accessing an unrelated volatile object does not by itself provide one for ordinary memory.
An integer pattern used to select bit positions for testing or modification. Its meaning on a device register must still follow that register access contract.
An integer operation, written & in C, whose result has a position set only when both operands have it set. This differs from the logical truth operator &&.
An integer operation, written | in C, whose result has a position set when either operand has it set. OR with a mask can set selected positions in an ordinary integer.
An integer operation, written ^ in C, whose result has a position set when the operands differ there. XOR with a mask can toggle selected positions.
An integer operation, written ~ in C, that flips the bits of the promoted operand. The promoted type determines which representation participates.
An operator that combines or negates truth values. C logical AND and OR short-circuit: their second operand is evaluated only when needed for the result.
The integer operation written << in C that shifts towards higher bit positions. The shift amount and promoted operand type must satisfy the language rules.
An assignment operator such as |= or += that combines an operation with updating the left object. Its use does not make a multi-step shared update indivisible.
A sequence that reads a current value, computes a replacement and writes it back. Concurrent changes and special device register write meanings can make a generic sequence unsafe.
A register convention in which writing one to a selected bit clears the corresponding status. Writing back all the ones seen in a previous read can therefore clear unintended events.
A configurable digital pin interface used to sample an input or drive an output. Pin function, direction and electrical restrictions depend on the chip and board.
A pin configuration that samples an external digital level rather than acting as a normal driven output. Input voltage limits and optional pulls still matter.
A pin configuration used to drive a digital signal according to the selected hardware mode. It does not make the pin capable of powering an arbitrary load.
A pin configuration that routes a specialised peripheral signal rather than ordinary GPIO operation. The supported functions and routing are device-specific.
A condition in which an input does not strongly drive the connected signal. Without a suitable external driver or pull, the sampled level can be unreliable.
An input whose level is not established by a suitable driver or bias connection. Such an input must not be assumed to give a stable digital value.
A resistor connection that weakly biases a signal towards its permitted high reference. It can give a released switch input a defined high level in a suitable circuit.
A resistor connection that weakly biases a signal towards ground. Its suitability depends on the circuit and the device input characteristics.
A signal convention in which the low electrical level represents the active condition. A pull-up button connected to ground can use this convention.
A signal convention in which the high electrical level represents the active condition. Software must use the actual circuit convention rather than infer it from a pin number.
Repeated making and breaking of electrical contact while a mechanical switch changes state. It can produce multiple digital transitions for one intended press or release.
Filtering or interpreting a changing switch input so its transient contact activity does not become repeated application actions. The acceptance interval must suit the signal and required response.
A C aggregate type that groups named fields into one object. A pointer to a structure can access its fields using the -> operator.
The lifetime category normally used by an ordinary local C object. Its storage exists for the relevant block execution and is not kept alive by returning its address.
A C lifetime category in which an object exists for the execution of the program. It does not imply that its contents survive a power loss or reset.
The part of execution during which an object exists with storage reserved for it. Access outside that lifetime is not permitted in C.
The limits of the elements belonging to an array. An array with a given positive count has valid element indexes from zero through one less than that count.
A pointer value that does not refer to an object or function. A null check can reject it, but non-null alone does not prove that an address is valid for a desired access.
The C unsigned integer type used for object sizes and sizeof results. It is suitable for representing array element counts within the available object-size range.
The maximum number of elements that a storage region is allowed to hold under its interface contract. Passing a claimed capacity does not prove the pointer actually refers to that much live storage.
Obtaining storage during program execution through an allocation interface. Programs must handle allocation failure and clearly define who releases the storage.
A device that represents an analogue input with a finite digital code. Interpreting the code requires its transfer model, reference and electrical conditions.
The number of bits used to distinguish converter output codes. A finer nominal code spacing does not establish the accuracy or noise performance of the complete measurement.
Representing a range of possible input values with a finite set of output values or codes. An ideal bin model gives a code interval rather than a unique exact physical input.
The voltage scale used by a converter for its input-to-code relationship. Error or noise in the reference can affect the measurement even when the digital code has many bits.
The illustrative model used here that assigns each input to an interval whose lower boundary is at or below that input. A real converter may place transitions differently.
The difference in electrical potential between two points, measured in volts. A permitted input voltage is a device and circuit requirement, not a universal property of GPIO.
The rate at which electric charge passes a location, measured in amperes. A small MCU pin cannot be assumed to supply the current demanded by an arbitrary load.
The unit used to express electrical potential difference. Device limits and reference values must identify the two relevant points and operating conditions.
One thousandth of a volt. Small ADC code spacing expressed in millivolts is a resolution calculation, not an accuracy guarantee.
One thousandth of a second. A sampling or pulse interval must state the unit so a raw count is not confused with a duration.
The unit of frequency: one repeating cycle per second. A PWM frequency states how often the whole waveform repeats.
A digital output technique that changes the active fraction of a repeating pulse cycle. The pin still switches between levels unless an additional system turns that waveform into another response.
The fraction of a repeating cycle for which a signal is in its stated active condition. Its interpretation must specify active-high or active-low meaning.
The time from one repeating waveform position to the next corresponding position. It is one divided by the repetition frequency.
A hardware setting that derives a slower counter clock from another clock. The exact divider and counter mode determine peripheral timing.
A value checked against a running hardware counter to determine an event or output state. The peripheral mode defines its exact comparison and update behaviour.
A peripheral that produces an analogue output corresponding to a digital input code. PWM is a pulse-timing technique and does not by itself provide a steady analogue output.
The electrical opposition presented by the circuit driving an input. Together with the ADC input circuit it affects how quickly a sampled input can settle.
The interval and process by which a converter input sampling circuit acquires the signal before conversion. Required settling depends on the converter and its source circuit.
The circuit reference used when specifying signal voltages in these examples. Connecting signals still requires compatible voltage ranges and the documented circuit arrangement.

The GNU Compiler Collection, which documents its own treatment of C volatile accesses and other implementation-specific behaviour. A compiler implementation is one part of a complete target toolchain.
Another name declared for a C type using typedef. Naming a structure type does not allocate a new structure object by itself.

The relationship between analogue input values and converter output codes, including where code transitions occur. A simple ideal bin model may not match the transition placement or errors of a real device.
A C pointer that does not compare equal to a null pointer. This alone does not establish that it refers to a live object with the type, alignment and writable capacity needed for an access.
The position used to select an element of a C array, starting at zero. A valid element index is smaller than the number of elements; C does not generally check that bound for you.
Storage whose capacity is chosen in advance and does not grow while it is used. The caller and receiving function must still respect its actual capacity, lifetime and ownership.
A sample's position in a sequence, counted from zero in these C examples. The index identifies an observation; converting it to elapsed time also requires the sampling schedule.

The rule a hardware timer follows as it moves through its count values, such as counting up and wrapping or counting up and then down. The selected mode changes how clock and comparison settings map to a PWM waveform.
